setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError silently no-ops when the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note is absent, and the new passkey re-auth path sets the context user without any writer of that note, allowing the user to switch identity mid-re-authentication via the editable username field, defeating prompt=login's same-user guarantee

The same inverted user-non-null gate in `authenticate()` (lines ~113-116) replaces the old `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` setup for not-yet-identified users, which is only masked on initial render by the conditional-UI execution but not on the error re-challenge

`UsernameForm.java` re-auth skip is gated purely on realm-level passkey enablement with no visible user-credential check, so password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms now see the username form on every prompt=login re-authentication where they previously skipped through (unverified whether `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` helper already checks user credentials)

Cross-class hand-maintained convention between `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (writer) and `AuthenticatorUtils` (reader) for the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note: `Boolean.parseBoolean` silently returns false on differently-cased or divergent truthy values, silently re-enabling registration UI on re-auth error pages

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm has no visible webauthnAuth field, so what 'conditional passkeys enabled' means on this path is undefined by the diff, and no test exercises UsernameForm, leaving the gate with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The claim that “no test exercises UsernameForm” is contradicted by the diff adding a new test in `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` (`webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), which is specifically for the username-form-based flow. Also, the assertion that the meaning of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is “undefined” because `UsernameForm` has no visible `webauthnAuth` field cannot be verified from this diff: the method may be defined in `UsernameForm`’s superclass or elsewhere (not shown in the patch), so the diff alone doesn’t establish that it’s undefined/broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The added !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() condition silently drops re-authentication via linked identity brokers: passkeys-enabled realms now skip the hasLinkedBrokers branch, leaving broker-linked users stuck at the username form with no IDP redirect, uncovered by tests

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the new condition `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` only controls whether the username form is *skipped* (via `context.success()`). Previously, broker-linked users already did **not** take the `context.success()` path because `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` would be true, so they would still see the form. With the change, when conditional passkeys are enabled, the code simply stops skipping the form for *any* identified user; it does not add logic that would block IDP options or prevent redirects, and nothing in the diff shows that IDP redirect depends on the `hasLinkedBrokers` check. The claim that broker-linked users are now “stuck … with no IDP redirect” is not demonstrated by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:113-117 inverts the user-null condition so fillContextForm is no longer invoked on the initial anonymous render of the login page, dropping WebAuthn form attributes (challenge/timeout/conditional-UI script data) for first-visit users; same inversion appears in challenge()
No test asserts conditional-UI presence on the very first anonymous render of the username/password form — tests were changed to assert the webauth form only after username submission

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple tests asserting the WebAuthn/conditional-UI form is present immediately after the initial anonymous render (i.e., right after `oauth.openLoginForm()` and before any username submission). For example, in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithExternalKey()` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication()`, the code does `oauth.openLoginForm(); ... loginPage.assertCurrent(); MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), Matchers.notNullValue());` before submitting a username. So it is not true that tests only assert presence after username submission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 calls no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that doesn't exist in its class hierarchy; helper exists only in sibling class UsernamePasswordForm, so the diff does not compile

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now calls `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg). However, the diff does not show the full `UsernameForm` class (or its superclass) to verify whether such a method exists elsewhere in that file or its hierarchy. While `UsernamePasswordForm` adds a different helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)`, the claim that the no-arg method “doesn’t exist in its class hierarchy” cannot be confirmed from the provided diff alone, so a compile break is not verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 forces the username form during re-authentication for every user in passkeys-enabled realms, even users with no WebAuthn credentials, discarding the original skip-form contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to skip the username form on re-authentication only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. This means that when conditional passkeys are enabled, the prior “skip username form when user is already set” behavior no longer applies, and the username form will be shown even in re-authentication scenarios regardless of whether the user actually has WebAuthn credentials (there’s no per-user credential check in this condition). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/contract change, but the diff doesn’t demonstrate it breaks correctness (it appears intentional to support passkeys re-auth flows), so it’s better treated as a review-worthy design/UX concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasLinkedBrokers is short-circuited out, so users with linked IDPs lose the broker re-authentication path

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` logic is still present and unchanged inside the re-auth shortcut block; the diff only adds an additional guard `&& !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` before entering that block. That means `hasLinkedBrokers` is not “short-circuited out” in general, and the diff does not show that users with linked IDPs lose a broker re-authentication path—if anything, when conditional passkeys are enabled the code simply avoids skipping the form even when `context.getUser()!=null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers a passkeys-enabled realm with a user lacking passkey credentials; reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey runs with passkeys disabled, testing the wrong configuration

adjudication.rationale: The new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` explicitly configures the realm with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and then asserts that WebAuthn UI is absent during `prompt=login` re-authentication. This does not cover the scenario “realm has passkeys enabled but the current user lacks any passkey credentials”. In the diff, other added tests exercise re-authentication when passkeys are enabled and the user does have passkeys (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication*`, `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), but none show passkeys enabled + user without passkeys. So the finding correctly identifies a specific missing edge-case test rather than a functional defect in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) conflates realm policy with user-identification state by returning false when user == null, so first-factor login page no longer calls fillContextForm() and the method name misleads
The deleted original comment documenting the 'user not already selected' invariant is not replaced anywhere

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace/update the removed comment. In `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` and `challenge`, the old comment about "user is not already selected" is replaced with new comments (e.g., "setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled" / "when possible") and the invariant is now encoded in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which explicitly requires `user != null`. So it’s not accurate to say the comment was deleted without replacement anywhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test assertions using try/catch around findElement with assertThat(..., nullValue()) are dead code passing only by accident of swallowed NoSuchElementException, instead of the correct assertThrows idiom used by sibling tests

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the new checks use `try { MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected..."); } catch (Exception ...) { /* expected */ }`. `findElement(...)` never returns null; it returns a WebElement or throws (typically NoSuchElementException). Therefore the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` is effectively dead/incorrect and the test passes only via the swallowed exception, whereas sibling tests in this diff use explicit `Assert.assertThrows(...)` for this pattern. This is a real, diff-grounded test-quality issue, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted guard on fillContextForm (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null) means UsernamePasswordForm no longer sets up webauthn/conditional-UI data on the initial login page in authenticate and both challenge overloads; correctness silently depends on a separate WebAuthn conditional-UI execution in the flow, and realms using UsernamePasswordForm with passkeys enabled but without that execution lose passkey autofill

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly inverts the condition for invoking `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`: in `challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String, String)` it changes from `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())` to `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. That means the webauthn/passkeys form context will no longer be set up on initial username+password login pages where `context.getUser()` is typically null. The same inversion is applied in `authenticate()` (moved call guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`). This is a concrete behavioral regression: passkeys/conditional-UI data won’t be prepared unless some other flow execution does it beforehand, matching the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError silently no-ops when the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note is absent, and the new passkey re-auth path sets the context user without any writer of that note, allowing the user to switch identity mid-re-authentication via the editable username field, defeating prompt=login's same-user guarantee

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError()` reading the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note and no-op’ing when it’s absent (`Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` -> `false`). However, this behavior is not new: the previous inline logic in `badPasswordHandler()` was gated by `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)`, which (by implication) would also be false when the note wasn’t set. The diff does not show any “new passkey re-auth path” that sets `context.getUser()` without also setting that note, nor does it show that the username field becomes editable specifically in re-auth in a way that defeats `prompt=login`. Those claims depend on code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Three parallel hand-maintained 'passkeys enabled' predicates (UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled()) already disagree in shape and must be kept in sync; future rule changes risk divergent behavior, and UsernamePasswordForm's method name is misleading since it means 'passkeys enabled AND user known' not conditional UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/uses multiple separate predicates for when passkeys/conditional UI should apply: `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` (requires `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` *and* `user != null`), `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.isPasskeysEnabled()` (feature+realm policy only, no user), and `UsernameForm` now gates behavior on `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (method body not shown here, but it is a distinct call site). These conditions are not unified and at least two clearly differ in shape (user-known requirement vs not), meaning future rule changes could diverge across classes. This is a maintainability/consistency concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone; also the name `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` is arguably misleading since it encodes "user known" as well as passkeys enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators to return false, bypassing the empty-authenticators early-out, so fillContextForm activates conditional-UI autofill for users with no passkey credential, causing a conditional-mediation request that can never succeed and showing a 'try passkey' affordance to password-only users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates the “build authenticators list / empty-authenticators early-out” logic behind `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that hook to always return `false`. This means Conditional UI will skip the `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` creation and its `isEmpty()` early-return path entirely (previously triggered whenever `context.getUser() != null`). However, the finding’s downstream claim (that this *necessarily* causes conditional-mediation to be triggered for password-only users and exposes a ‘try passkey’ affordance that can never succeed) is not directly verifiable from the provided diff because the rest of `fillContextForm()` (what attributes/buttons it sets when skipping the authenticators block) is not shown. What is verifiable is a behavior/UX risk: bypassing the empty-authenticator check could allow Conditional UI setup even when the identified user has no WebAuthn credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In UsernamePasswordForm.java:110-115, the guard isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) inverts the original semantics: fillContextForm is now called only when user != null, so on the first anonymous render the conditional passkey autofill UI is never set up; same inverted guard exists in challenge(context, error, field) (~line 136)
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both point out that gating fillContextForm/conditional passkey setup on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user != null) prevents the conditional passkey UI from being initialized on the initial login page when context.getUser() is still null, breaking ID-less/first-time passkey login. Candidate also notes the same pattern in challenge().

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:196-201 silently flips a behavioral assertion: old test asserted NoSuchElementException for the webauthn form once user was identified, new test asserts the opposite, reversing product behavior for users whose only passkey is non-discoverable who now see a passkey UI that errors when used

adjudication.rationale: The test assertion in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest is indeed flipped (it now expects the `//form[@id='webauth']` element to be present after username is identified). However, the diff also changes product code to intentionally keep/show passkeys UI when a user is already set (e.g., `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` now requires `user != null`, and `fillContextForm`/`challenge` call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm` in that case). Additional tests are added specifically to ensure passkeys work during re-authentication (prompt=login). The claimed negative behavior (“UI that errors when used” for non-discoverable-only passkeys) is not verifiable from this diff: there’s no evidence here that the UI errors or that behavior is regressed beyond the intentional change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 uses !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() based on realm policy, not per-user credentials, forcing password-only users through a username form step on re-auth that advertises passkey UI that cannot succeed for them

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `UsernameForm.authenticate()` changing to skip the username form on re-authentication only when `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, but it does not show the implementation of `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` nor any code here that ties it specifically to “realm policy only” vs “per-user credentials”. The claim that this forces password-only users through a step that “advertises passkey UI that cannot succeed” is also not directly verifiable from this diff (whether passkey UI is shown when a user has no WebAuthn credentials depends on logic not shown here, e.g., how the form decides to render webauthn elements).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey claims to test that passkeys are unavailable for users without a passkey, but only disables the realm-wide passkeys policy; the per-user credential scenario is never exercised and the code shows passkey UI to passkey-less users during re-auth

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` explicitly sets the realm-wide policy `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and the test comment says it’s about passkeys being disabled for the realm (“passkeys is not enabled for the realm”), not about a per-user “no passkey credential” scenario. The test then asserts the WebAuthn form is absent both on initial login and on prompt=login re-auth, which matches the realm-disabled setup. The finding’s claim that the test purports to cover a per-user passkey-less scenario (but doesn’t) misreads the test’s stated purpose. The additional claim that “the code shows passkey UI to passkey-less users during re-auth” isn’t verifiable from the provided diff alone (no diff-grounded evidence of UI shown to users without credentials).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses an exception-swallowing try/catch pattern where the fail() is unreachable dead code; if refactored to return a value instead of throwing, the check passes unconditionally — should use driver.findElements().isEmpty() directly

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey, the test checks absence of the webauthn form via `try { driver.findElement(...); ... fail(); } catch (Exception ...) {}`. As written, `driver.findElement(...)` never returns null, so `assertThat(..., nullValue())` cannot succeed, making the subsequent `fail()` effectively unreachable in the “element present” path (the assertion would throw an AssertionError, not caught). The pattern relies on exceptions for control flow and is brittle; using `findElements(...).isEmpty()` would be a clearer, non-exception-based absence check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey never asserts the re-auth form state (USERNAME_HIDDEN=true, REGISTRATION_DISABLED=true, attempted username, re-auth form rather than fresh form), so a regression of setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to a no-op would still pass all new tests

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, after triggering re-authentication via prompt=login, the test only asserts the info message and presence of the webauthn form, then proceeds with password-only logins (e.g., loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"))) and webauthn link clicks. It never directly asserts the re-auth UI/form state that setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is meant to enforce (e.g., LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes, attempted username/preserved user). Thus a regression where AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError becomes a no-op could plausibly still allow these tests to pass (at least without detecting the specific re-auth form-state behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new AuthenticUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (passkey-failure error path during re-auth) has no test coverage; a passkey assertion failure during re-auth could expose the username field unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context);` in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`, i.e., specifically on the passkey-failure error path. The tests added/modified in this PR focus on successful passkey re-authentication (`webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`) and on password-failure during re-authentication while ensuring the WebAuthn button remains visible. None of the added tests appear to exercise the conditional-passkey failure path that would invoke `createErrorResponse(...)` and therefore validate that the username is kept hidden/registration disabled during re-auth via the new helper. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-coverage concern rather than a functional defect (the code change itself is intended to prevent the exposure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernameFormTest / PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication performs no assertion that a login form / conditional-UI element appeared before appPage, so it cannot distinguish a form-rendered re-auth from silent re-login without UI

adjudication.rationale: In both newly added tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` (in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`), after `oauth.openLoginForm()` and after the `prompt=login` re-auth step, the test immediately does `appPage.assertCurrent()` and validates only the login event. There is no assertion that any login UI (e.g., `loginPage.assertCurrent()` or presence of a conditional-UI/WebAuthn element) was shown before reaching the app. So the test does not explicitly distinguish a UI-driven conditional-passkeys re-auth flow from an immediate redirect back to the app due to some other behavior (e.g., SSO reuse), beyond the event expectation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey re-auth check lacks an explicit CREDENTIAL_TYPE assertion (only USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED nullValue), making it weaker than the established pattern used elsewhere in the same file (detail(CREDENTIAL_TYPE, nullValue()))

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the login event assertion only checks `.detail(WebAuthnConstants.USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED, nullValue())` and omits an explicit `.detail(Details.CREDENTIAL_TYPE, nullValue())`. Elsewhere in the same file (e.g., `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) the established pattern includes asserting `Details.CREDENTIAL_TYPE` is `nullValue()` for password logins. This makes the new test less strict/diagnostic, but it is a test-strength issue rather than a functional defect in the product code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten `challenge(context, error, field)` gate `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires `user != null`, making the regular-login branch dead code; after one wrong password submission the re-rendered combined username/password page loses the passkey/conditional-UI affordance (fillContextForm no longer re-invoked), silently funneling users into password-only retry

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`, the diff changes the condition from `context.getUser() == null && ... isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This makes `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` never run when the user is *not* set on the context (a case the previous code explicitly handled, per the comment “when the user is not already selected”). If the flow clears `context.getUser()` on a bad password (a behavior implied by the existence of the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` note and re-authentication special casing), the subsequent re-rendered challenge would no longer re-populate passkey/conditional-UI form attributes, matching the reported regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The same inverted user-non-null gate in `authenticate()` (lines ~113-116) replaces the old `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` setup for not-yet-identified users, which is only masked on initial render by the conditional-UI execution but not on the error re-challenge

`UsernameForm.java` re-auth skip is gated purely on realm-level passkey enablement with no visible user-credential check, so password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms now see the username form on every prompt=login re-authentication where they previously skipped through (unverified whether `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` helper already checks user credentials)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `UsernameForm.authenticate()` changes the re-authentication fast-path from `if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`. This is a concrete behavior change: when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true, the authenticator will no longer skip the username form even if the user is already set (e.g., prompt=login re-auth). However, the finding’s assertion that `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is *purely* realm-level and lacks any user-credential check cannot be verified from this diff because the implementation of `UsernameForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is not shown here. So the risk/regression is diff-grounded, but the root cause stated (no user-credential check) is not directly provable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-class hand-maintained convention between `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (writer) and `AuthenticatorUtils` (reader) for the `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note: `Boolean.parseBoolean` silently returns false on differently-cased or divergent truthy values, silently re-enabling registration UI on re-auth error pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`, which reads an auth note and uses `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)` to decide whether to hide username/disable registration. However, the finding’s core claim that `Boolean.parseBoolean` “silently returns false on differently-cased” truthy values is incorrect: `Boolean.parseBoolean` is case-insensitive for the string "true". The diff also does not show any writer setting divergent truthy values (e.g., "1", "yes"), so the alleged cross-class convention break and resulting UI behavior regression cannot be verified from the shown changes.
